# 4 Maccabees Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Praise of Eleazar

---

**7:1** O man of blessed old age, of venerable gray hair and law-devoted life, sealed by the faithful death of martyrdom!

**7:2** If the old age of Eleazar had yielded for a brief time out of piety — if he had saved his life — he would have shown that old age is dishonored, not honored, by religion.

**7:3** But he has made old age truly honored by having it sealed in the fidelity of martyrdom.

**7:4** He proved that among the people who are devoted to piety, old age is a thing of beauty — not when it shrinks from danger but when it stands firm in it.

**7:5** What is more admirable: that reason held its place above the passions in this man, or that the law proved itself a ruler of passions through him?

**7:6** Eleazar the priest — ninety years of age, that body already spent with old age, that flesh consumed by torments — proved by his victory that reason is sovereign over the passions.

**7:7** O you who prevailed over the tyrant through the strength of your reasoning, and who overcame the cruelties of all their torments by your endurance!

**7:8** Just as our father Aaron, armed with the censer, ran through the midst of the congregation on fire, and conquered the fiery angel by the power of prayer,

**7:9** so too did Eleazar, who was consumed in fire, prove by his willingness to die that reason strengthened by piety can extinguish even the fire of the passions.

**7:10** Most admirable also was this: although his body was already broken by age and his sinews were slack, he renewed his youthful strength through reason and nullified the power of the rack.

**7:11** O noble father, old man of great deeds, holy elder of the law! You did not flinch when surrounded by the instruments of torture!

**7:12** You did not shrink from the blows of whips! You did not surrender under the agony of the burning!

**7:13** You remained supremely faithful to the holy name of God and continued your piety until death!

**7:14** O priest who truly served God, O guardian of the holy law, O preserver of devotion to God!

**7:15** Though your body was being tortured with fire, your soul clung to the sacred purpose of the law.

**7:16** Your courage and self-mastery proved beyond any doubt that reason can govern the passions.

**7:17** For the enemies themselves were filled with wonder as they saw you in the midst of their torments.

**7:18** Even the tyrant and all his court marveled at your endurance.

**7:19** And this brought no small honor upon your nation and upon the divine law.

**7:20** After Eleazar's death, the seven brothers were brought forward, along with their mother, to the same test.

**7:21** They are brothers who, having been educated in the same law and trained in the same devotion, were in every way worthy of the venerable old priest.

**7:22** Their mother, seeing all this, urged them on with courage, speaking to them in their ancestral language: My children, noble is the struggle, and having been summoned to it for the testimony of our nation, fight zealously for the law of our fathers.

**7:23** She ended: And it would be unreasonable for me, who made you lovers of your souls, to be grieved for you now.
